newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse to start trading again, 3 banks list.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse to start trading again, 3 banks list.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) expects three banks to list and start selling their shares on the bourse soon, a BSE official said on Monday.

"Three banks have filed requests to the BSE to list their shares totalling 21 million dinars ($3.89 million) and the listing procedure should be finalised soon," BSE general manager Pava Zecevic told reporters.

Based on the Yugoslav Securities Commission (YSC) approval, Niska banka will place 12 million dinars worth of shares on the BSE, Kulska banka five million and Panonska banka four million dinars of its new stock, Zecevic said.
Vojvodjanska banka will be entrusted with the sale of stock of Niska and Kulska banka, while the largest Yugoslav brokerage Trziste Novca has been selected for Panonska banka.
"This could mark a crucial step in the development of the Yugoslav equities market," BSE spokesman Milko Stimac told Reuters.
"Those shares mean new instruments for the bourse and also a way towards portfolio diversification for local investors," Stimac added.

The BSE has not traded any shares since early 1996. The only two shares listed and traded in 1995 were those of Investbanka and Sintelon. Both shares were withdrawn from the listing late in 1996 after several months of non-trading.
